title: Roundup: Slaters get key win over MAU | Local | rutlandherald.com
text:
FAIR HAVEN — Whenever the Far Haven girls soccer team topples Division I Mount Anthony, it is considered a watershed win.
That is why there was so much joy at the Slaters' LaPlaca Field on Wednesday night. Leigha Kretzer knocked in two goals for a 2-0 halftime lead and Yakira Long banged in a corner kick that had been ping ponging around to cap off the 3-0 victory over the Patriots.
MAU's Ella Palisano was out with concussion protocol and Fair Haven coach Teri Perry said the absence of her speed gave the Slaters an edge.
"It definitely made a difference," Perry said.
"We knew that we had to be very aggressive and that we had to win the 50-50 balls and had to win those balls on direct kicks that don't always get to the place. I think we did a good job of that."
Fair Haven goalie Sophia Russell had a strong game.
The Slaters take a 2-2 record into Monday night's home game against Stratton Mountain School.
GIRLS SOCCER
Westside 8, LT 2
DORSET — The West Rutland girls soccer team remained unbeaten through its three games by beating Long Trail 8-2 on Wednesday.
Hayley Raiche had a hat trick and Emma Haley added two goals. Myra Rocke, Meredith Rocke and Izzy Griffith also scored for the Golden Horde.
Westside's eighth grade goalie Emma Harte garnered five saves.
"She played well," West Rutland coach Deanna Rodolfy said.
West Rutland (3-0) hosts Poultney on Friday.
MSJ 8, Randolph 0
RANDOLPH — Mount St. Joseph coach Liz Yaddow appreciated a game with a lot of breathing room after the previous nail-biter that went into the second overtime in a win over Poultney.
This time the Mounties whipped Randolph 8-0 with Riley Collins scoring four of the goals and Jada Hughes two. Defender Abby Williams had a goal as did Greta Courcelle. Maddie Drude contributed an assist.
MSJ keeper Ivy Crowley earned shutout with seven saves.
The Mounties will take a 3-1 record into the Arlington's John Werner Tournament on Tuesday.
TV 1, Mill River 0
(Overtime)
WILMINGTON — Alejandra Bevilacqua scored the night's only goal at Hayford Field as Twin Valley defeated Mill River 1-0 in overtime.
The Wildcats improved their record to 2-1 and Mill River fell to 0-3.
BOYS SOCCER
Montpelier 5, RHS 1
MONTPELIER — A four-goal flurry in a span of 14 minutes allowed Montpelier to play with house money down the stretch during Wednesday’s 5-1 boys soccer victory over Rutland.
Rutland’s Ciaran Wiezalis opened the scoring in the 34th minute and then Montpelier’s Will Curis equalized in the 39th minute, resulting in a 1-1 tie entering halftime.
“It was a great response after going down by a goal,” MHS coach Eric Bagley said. “It was a pretty even game leading up to their goal. And then Will scoring just before halftime helped turn the tide and gave us some nice momentum going into the second half.”
Winter Holloway scored what proved to be the game-winner on a Cyrus Gendron assist in the 59th minute. Curtis extended the lead to 3-1 in the 65th minute on a pass from Dean Jones and then Curtis scored again in the 72nd minute off a feed from Dax Desharnis. A minute later, Jones capped the scoring with an unassisted effort after he pounced on a ball that bounced off a Rutland defender.
Julian Leendertse made six saves for MHS, while Colin Rider stopped eight shots for Rutland.
Montpelier (3-1) will host U-32 at 6 p.m. Tuesday. Rutland (1-3) will host Mount Anthony on Sept. 17 at 6 p.m.
GOLF
Serafin medals
SPRINGFIELD — Mill River senior Mattie Serafin picked up another medalist honor, shooting a 36 in Wednesday's match at Crown Point Country Club.
Serafin tied for the medalist honor with Stevens' Owen Wilkinson, who also shot a 36. Windsor's Jake Smith shot a 37.
Hartford was the winning team shooting a 169. The Hurricanes' top golfer was Thomas Thorburn, shooting a 39. Sam Grigsby was close behind at 41.
Host Springfield was led by Chase Strong, shooting a 50.
FIELD HOCKEY
BBA 2, Fair Haven 1
MANCHESTER — The Burr and Burton Academy field hockey team got goals from Marlee Gallagher and Fiona Corbett to build a 2-0 lead but Quinn Murphy, with an assist from Riley Babbie, with 1:14l left in the contest made it a one-goal game.
Three BBA goalies — Marlee Clark, Emily Abbot and Emma Anderson — did not have a single save among them.
Victoria Kelly was extremelt busy at the other end to the tune of 16 saves.
"This was a more one-sided game than the score indicates," BBA coach Barb Miceli said. "The goalie saves tell a more accurate story. We had 18 offensive penalty corners to their one, but their defense was tough. They were aggressive to the ball the whole way.
"We had a great game from Marlee Gallagher at right midfield and from Fiona Corbett at left midfield. Belle Grattan made a lot of things happen offensively for us as well."
Grattan and Ella Kruczala earned assists on the game's first goal.
The Bulldogs will take a 4-0 record into Wednesday's home game against Bellows Falls.
Hartford 5, Rutland 0
Rutland is 0-4 and still looking for its first goal of the season after Wednesday's 5-0 blanking by Hartford.
The good news: The Hurricanes led 5-0 at halftime and Rutland coach Tammy Landon said her team "played their best half of field hockey" while keeping them off the board those final 30 minutes.
"I was very happy. She (Heather Scudder) played a lot of players in the second half but we did play a lot better. We really settled in," Landon said.
"We also had a little offense."
Landon praised Kinsley Rodrigue and Savannah Wade for strong games and showing a lot of progress.
She also said her goalie Sam Cacace turned in another strong performance.
RHS is off until Wednesday when Otter Valley comes to town.
WOMEN'S SOCCER
RPI 1, Castleton 0
CASTLETON — The VTSU Castleton women's soccer team fell to Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute 1-0 on Wednesday night at Dave Wolk Stadium.
Annabelle Bachhuber scored the game's lone goal in the 50th minute.
Fair Haven's Emma Ezzo made 13 saves for the Spartans in the loss.
Castleton (0-4) is at Western Connecticut on Saturday.
